statement: statement: Exact characteristic-vector residual update for membership streaming. Let F⊆{0,1}^N. At cut t, encode a prefix p by the characteristic vector z_p∈{0,1}^{2^{N−t}} of R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}, with coordinates indexed by suffixes u. For t<N, on input bit b, the next state has coordinates z'_{v}=(¬b∧z_{0v})∨(b∧z_{1v}) for every v∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}. Thus the update is realizable with one shared NOT gate for b and at most 3·2^{N−t−1} AND/OR gates. The terminal state decides membership by testing its sole coordinate. Proof: By definition, R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv∈R_t(p)}. Its v-coordinate is therefore z_p[bv], which equals z_{0v} if b=0 and z_{1v} if b=1. The displayed Boolean multiplexer computes exactly this coordinate; each uses two AND gates and one OR gate, with ¬b shared. At t=N the residual is {ε} for members and empty for nonmembers, so the final bit is the membership answer. Scope: a time-varying, exponentially wide representation for decision streaming; it gives no fixed-(S,D) Pareto result and no full-search decoder bound.

statement: statement: Shared-minterm transition upper bound. Let T be any partial deterministic transition from a reachable subset A of {0,1}^4 × {0,1} to {0,1}^4. With fan-out allowed and gates NOT, binary AND, and binary OR, T has an extension to all 32 inputs implemented with at most 257 gates, counting five shared input negations and allowing constants. Proof: For each of the 32 input patterns z, build its equality indicator h_z as the AND of its five input literals; the five negations are shared, and each indicator costs four AND gates, for 128 gates total. For each of the four output bits, OR the indicators h_z for patterns whose extended output bit is 1, using at most 31 OR gates. This costs at most 124 more gates. On every reachable input the selected indicator is exactly its pattern’s indicator, so the output equals T. Total: 5+128+124=257. The bound applies in particular to any S=4 SC_{3,1} transition, but does not determine its minimum G_max.

label: S0387
statement: statement: Shared-factoring transition upper bound at S=4. Let A be any subset of {0,1}^4×{0,1}, and let T:A→{0,1}^4 be any partial deterministic transition. With fan-out allowed and gates NOT, binary AND, and binary OR, T extends to a total function on {0,1}^5 computable with at most 173 gates, allowing constants. Proof: Extend T arbitrarily outside A. Negate the five input bits once (5 NOT gates), so every input literal is available. For the first two inputs, construct all four two-literal conjunctions (4 AND gates). For the last three inputs, construct all four conjunctions of the first two of those three literals (4 AND gates), then combine each with either polarity of the fifth literal, obtaining all eight three-literal conjunctions (8 AND gates). Combine each of the four two-literal terms with each of the eight three-literal terms to obtain all 32 five-literal minterms (32 AND gates). For each of four output coordinates, OR the minterms on which that coordinate is 1, using at most 31 binary OR gates; if the set is empty, use constant 0. The total is 5+4+4+8+32+4·31=173. Each input activates exactly its own minterm, so the output equals the chosen extension and therefore T on A. This is a universal upper bound and leaves the exact minimum for SC_{3,1} unresolved.

statement:
statement: For every n>=3, the family A_n of truth tables of affine Boolean functions f(x)=a_0 XOR sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i, in lexicographic input order, has a deterministic one-pass streaming recognizer with a final witness decoder, S=n+2 state bits, and zero charged update gates. Proof: Store the first n+1 input bits of the stream in n+1 state coordinates, leaving the marker coordinate z=0 on live prefixes. While t<=n+1, each update copies prior coordinates and writes the next stream bit into the next sample coordinate; after t=n+1, retain the sample coordinates. Each update coordinate is therefore a wire or the new input bit. The values at inputs 0,e_1,...,e_n uniquely determine the affine coefficients, so at each layer t<=n+1 distinct live prefixes have distinct samples, and for t>n+1 distinct live prefixes correspond to distinct affine functions and thus distinct samples. For t>n+1, assign each dead prefix a state with z=1, disjoint from all live states. At t<=n+1 every prefix is live, since the first t evaluations are independent affine linear forms. At the end, the decoder reconstructs the affine function from the sample, compares its full table with the input, outputs its coefficients on a match, and rejects otherwise. Since n+2<2^n for n>=3, this is below the input length. This proves the affine zero-update-gate control construction only; it says nothing about SC_{n,s} or P versus NP.
scope: Every n>=3; affine Boolean truth tables of length 2^n in lexicographic order; deterministic layered transducer; S=n+2; fixed unrestricted final decoder; update coordinates restricted to wires/copies of old state or new input; dead-prefix separation where dead prefixes exist.

statement:
statement: Universal truth-table update construction. Let S>=0 and F:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S be a state-update map on S state bits and one arriving input bit. With fan-in-two AND/OR gates, free NOT, constants, and unrestricted fan-out, F has a circuit with at most S(S*2^{S+1}+2^{S+1}-1) counted gates. For S=4 this is 636. This upper bound applies to a specified update map; it does not prove an S=4 encoding exists for SC_{3,1} or determine minimum G_max.
proof: For each output coordinate j, form one minterm for every input a with F_j(a)=1. Each minterm is a conjunction of S+1 literals and uses S binary AND gates. There are at most 2^{S+1} minterms, whose disjunction uses at most 2^{S+1}-1 binary OR gates. The empty disjunction is constant 0. Thus each output uses at most S*2^{S+1}+2^{S+1}-1 gates. Constructing all S output coordinates separately gives the stated bound. Each output agrees with its truth table on every input, so the circuit computes F exactly.

statement:
statement: Sparse truth-table implementation bound. For every integer S>=0 and every map F:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S, with fan-in-two AND/OR gates, free NOT, constants, and unrestricted fan-out, F is computable using at most S((S+1)2^S-1) counted gates. In particular, for S=4 the bound is 316. This is an upper bound for a specified update map; it does not assert existence of an S=4 streaming encoding for SC_{3,1} or determine its minimum G_max.
proof: Let k=S+1 and consider one output coordinate f. If its 1-set has r elements, its DNF has r minterms, each a conjunction of k literals and hence uses k-1 binary AND gates; combining r terms uses r-1 OR gates. Its cost is at most kr-1 when r>0. Alternatively, write a DNF for the 0-set and negate its output at zero NOT cost; if that set has q>0 elements, the cost is at most kq-1. If either set is empty, f is a constant and costs zero. Since min(r,q)<=2^{k-1}=2^S, a nonconstant f costs at most k*2^S-1=(S+1)2^S-1. Implement each of the S output coordinates separately and sum the bounds. The resulting circuits compute each coordinate's truth table exactly, hence compute F exactly. For S=0 there are no output coordinates, so the zero-gate bound also holds.

label: S0192
statement: PROCEDURE UPD (exact bit-streaming update of the EXT prefix automaton, claimed by R1460). Setting: N = 2^m, Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs (gate lists, output = last gate), totally ordered by list index ord. Truth tables Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. The state after reading prefix p of length t is w(p) = ord-least C with Eval(C) starting with p, if one exists. STATE: the single circuit w (encoding O(s log(m+s)) bits) plus the counter t (log N bits). CLAIM: UPD(w, b) := ord-least C in Circ_s with Eval(C)[0..t] = Eval(w)[0..t-1] . b computes w(pb) exactly. PROOF: (i) Eval(w)[0..t-1] = p, since w(p) starts with p by definition, so p is recoverable from the state. (ii) {C : Eval(C) starts with pb} = {C : Eval(C) starts with p and Eval(C)_t = b} is exactly the set the scan tests, so the scan returns min S(pb) = w(pb). (iii) If no C matches, S(pb) is empty and the stream is dead. RUNNING TIME: scanning costs at most |Circ_s| candidates; each prefix test evaluates a candidate on assignments 0..t, which is O((t+1) s) word operations. With |Circ_s| <= 2(16(m+s)^2)^s (each gate: 16 ops and at most (m+s)^2 operand pairs), one bit costs O((16(m+s)^2)^s (t+1) s) operations and N bits cost O((16(m+s)^2)^s N^2 s). SCOPE: exact for every m, s; the time is polynomial in N for fixed s but exponential in s, so it does NOT give poly(s) per-bit update and does NOT close G0004 or G0003. It shows that the update function is computable from the O(s log(m+s))-bit state plus t, with an explicit bound. OPEN: whether the scan over Circ_s can be replaced by a search of size poly(s) (this is the content of G0004).

label: S0198
statement: PROCEDURE (restricted case s=1, bookkeeping, closes no obligation). Index truth tables of m-bit inputs by x in {0,1}^m as an integer in 0..N-1, N=2^m, and let bit t be the value at index t. Let Im_1 be the truth tables of all nodes of circuits of size at most 1: the m projections and g(x_i,x_j) for the 16 binary Boolean functions g and i,j in [m]; |Im_1| <= m + 16 m^2. Let C_t = {f in Im_1 : first t bits of f equal the prefix p}, C_0 = Im_1. Appending bit b keeps the f in C_t whose bit t equals b. Each bit t of g(x_i,x_j) is read from x_i and x_j in O(m) time, so one update costs O(m^3) time, and the state is O(m^2 log m) bits. Correctness: p is in P_t iff some f in Im_1 has prefix p, and C_t is exactly that set by definition. Scope: s=1 only; the general update-time obligation (poly(s) per bit for all s) is not addressed.

label: S0208
statement: PROC-U (space-bounded exact update, no stored witness). Setting: Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size at most s on m inputs, each a sequence of at most s gates (op in 16, two operand indices among earlier nodes), encoded in O(s log(m+s)) bits; ord = the enumeration order by increasing index. Eval(C) in {0,1}^N, N = 2^m. For a bit string x of length t+1 <= N, define SCAN(x): enumerate Circ_s in ord, compute Eval(C) for each C, return the first C whose first t+1 bits equal x, or NONE. CLAIM 1 (correctness): SCAN(x) returns the ord-least C with prefix x, i.e. w(x) as defined in S0095, or NONE iff x is not live. Proof: the enumeration visits Circ_s in ord, so the first match is the least match. CLAIM 2 (space): the enumerator is a mixed-radix counter over gate sequences of length at most s, using O(s log(m+s)) bits of workspace plus O(log N) for the index t. CLAIM 3 (time): |Circ_s| <= sum_{k<=s} (16 (m+s)^2)^k <= 2 (16 (m+s)^2)^s, and each Eval costs O(s N / w) word operations. Hence the update of the prefix automaton state p -> pb (computed as SCAN(pb), without any stored state) takes time at most 2 (16(m+s)^2)^s * O(s N) = 2^{O(s log(m+s))} * N^{O(1)}, workspace O(s log(m+s)) bits. SCOPE: an upper bound on update time for the exact EXT automaton; it is NOT poly(s) time, so it does NOT close G0004. It is the space-honest baseline: the cm-363c62d5d38d4b6f check used a precomputed Im list, which is not poly-space, so that run does not verify this claim. Any per-bit update-time lower bound for total Search-MCSP must lie below this 2^{O(s log(m+s))} N^{O(1)} upper bound to be non-trivial.

statement: Restricted-size EXT streaming procedure. Fix n and a constant s0. Let C_{n,s0} be a fixed-length padded list of all Boolean circuits on n inputs with at most s0 fan-in-two gates, with each circuit's truth table ordered lexicographically on {0,1}^n. statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-set transition circuit). Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. For a truth-table prefix p of length t, store the M-bit vector v_t with v_t[d]=1 iff circuit d agrees with p on positions 0 through t-1, and an n-bit counter for t (the case t=2^n is handled by a separate terminal flag). On reading bit b, generate the n-bit input assignment x_t indexed by t, then for each d set v_{t+1}[d]=v_t[d] AND [f_d(x_t)=b], and advance the counter. For every t, the invariant v_t[d]=1 iff d agrees with p on its first t positions follows by induction: it holds initially because the empty prefix imposes no constraint, and the update retains exactly candidates whose next output equals b. Thus the update is exact and the prefix is extendible within the represented family iff some bit of v_t is 1. If generating x_t takes O(n) time and evaluating one listed circuit on x_t takes O(s) time, the update takes O(n+Ms) time and the mutable state uses M+n+O(1) bits; the fixed description list is read-only program data. Since a standard gate-list encoding has M <= 2^{O(s log(n+s))}, this is generally exponential in s and n. This procedure gives no lower bound for compressed or arbitrary representations, so it does not close G0004.
derivation: Use the stated candidate-membership invariant. At position t, compute the corresponding assignment once, evaluate each still-live circuit, and filter by equality with the arriving bit. The induction proves exactness. The stated time sums one O(n) assignment-generation cost and M evaluations of O(s) each; the stored membership vector and counter give the state bound.
scope: All finite n,s and any fixed explicit circuit list D under the stated costs. The universal update-computation lower bound for all representations remains open.

statement: SURVIVOR-BITSET TRANSITION FOR EXT. Fix n and a finite family D of Boolean circuits on n input bits, with |D|=M, and fix an ordering x_1,...,x_{2^n} of the truth-table inputs. For each prefix p of length t, let B_p be the M-bit vector whose d-coordinate is 1 exactly when circuit d's truth table begins with p. Given t, B_p, and the next bit b, B_{pb} is computed coordinatewise by (B_{pb})_d=(B_p)_d AND [d(x_{t+1})=b]. Thus the transition has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most 2M gates when the constants [d(x_{t+1})=b] are supplied for this fixed t,b; decoder acceptance is OR of the M coordinates. For EXT_{n,s}, take D to contain one representative for each n-input circuit of size at most s. This gives an exact, explicit transition procedure with M=|D| state bits and O(M) transition gates per fixed position. Proof: d survives prefix p exactly when its first t truth-table bits equal p. It survives the child prefix pb exactly when it survives p and its next truth-table bit equals b. The displayed coordinate formula is precisely this equivalence, independently for each d. OR of the coordinates is 1 exactly when some circuit in D extends p. No claim is made that this representation is minimal or polynomial in s.
derivation: Enumerate the finite circuit family D. Store one survivor bit per description. For each coordinate, update by AND with the fixed indicator that the circuit's next output bit equals b. By induction on prefix length, the stored coordinates are exactly the descriptions extending the current prefix. The decoder OR therefore recognizes EXT. Each coordinate uses at most one AND gate; a binary OR tree uses at most M−1 gates.
scope: All finite n, s, fixed circuit families D, and fixed truth-table input order. The transition circuit is position-specific (t is fixed in its constants); no bound polynomial in s is asserted. The state width M may be exponential in s log(n+s), and this does not establish a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: SURVIVOR SET IS A SUFFICIENT STATE FOR EXT. Fix n, a finite family D of Boolean circuits on n input bits, and an ordering x_1,...,x_{2^n} of the inputs. For a prefix p of length t, define S_p={d in D: d(x_i)=p_i for every 1<=i<=t}. Then (i) p is an extendible truth-table prefix iff S_p is nonempty; and (ii) for any next bit b, S_{pb}={d in S_p: d(x_{t+1})=b}. Proof: If p is extendible, by definition some d in D agrees with p at every listed position, so d lies in S_p; conversely any d in S_p supplies a completion, namely its remaining truth-table bits. For the transition identity, d belongs to S_{pb} exactly when it agrees with p on the first t positions and has value b at x_{t+1}, which is precisely membership in the displayed filtered set. Hence the survivor set, with nonemptiness as decoder, is an exact sufficient state for every prefix transition.
derivation: Both assertions follow by expanding the definition of S_p coordinatewise. Membership is exactly agreement with the prefix; appending b adds exactly one agreement condition.
scope: All finite n, all finite families D of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n (in particular circuit families), all input orders, all prefixes including t=0 and t=2^n. This is a sufficient-state lemma only; it gives no compact encoding or low-cost transition from H_C.

statement:
statement: EXACT CANDIDATE-SET STATE AND TRANSITION FOR EXT. Fix n,s and a finite set D of M circuit descriptions on n inputs, with truth tables indexed 0,...,N-1. After a prefix p of length t, encode the EXT state by the M-bit vector q_p whose coordinate q_p(d)=1 exactly when the truth table of d begins with p. At level t<N, on input next bit b, update each coordinate by q_{pb}(d)=q_p(d) AND [C_d(t)=b]. Because C_d(t) is a fixed bit for each d,t, this transition is implemented by at most M fan-in-two Boolean gates (indeed each coordinate either wires q_p(d) or outputs 0), with the level t and description set fixed. The accepting predicate is OR_d q_p(d), and is 1 exactly when p is an EXT prefix. Thus EXT has an exact deterministic layered streaming representation with M state bits and O(M) real gates per transition; this bound is polynomial in s only if M is.
derivation: Induct on prefix length t. At t=0 every description agrees with the empty prefix, so q_empty is the all-ones vector. Assume q_p(d)=1 iff C_d agrees with p at positions 0,...,t-1. The stated update retains d precisely when it also agrees at position t, hence q_pb(d)=1 iff C_d agrees with pb on all positions through t. This proves the invariant for every prefix. The output OR is true precisely when at least one such description exists, which is the definition of EXT_{n,s}(p). For a fixed level and description, C_d(t) is a constant; the coordinate update is either the identity wire (if that constant is b) or constant zero. This gives the asserted O(M) transition circuit and makes no polynomial-in-s assertion.
scope: All finite n,s and every fixed finite circuit-description set D; exact deterministic streaming representation measured in state bits and fan-in-two Boolean transition gates. It does not yield a polynomial-in-s bound when M is exponential, nor a representation for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0981
statement: statement: EXPLICIT EXT PREFIX-FILTER PROCEDURE. Fix n,s and enumerate ordered fan-in-two Boolean circuit descriptions with at most s gates, allowing AND, OR, NOT, constants and n input wires. Let M be their number. For a prefix p of the truth table in lexicographic input order, store exactly the descriptions whose outputs agree with p. Initially store all M descriptions. On appending the next truth-table bit, evaluate every retained circuit on the corresponding input and discard it if its output disagrees. After each update the retained list is exactly the circuits consistent with the new prefix; hence it is nonempty iff that prefix is extendible by the truth table of a circuit of size at most s. Each circuit evaluation costs O(s), so each transition costs O(Ms), and the explicit list uses O(Ms log(n+s)) bits under a standard encoding. The number M is at most (s+1)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s, by choosing at each of at most s topologically ordered gates a type and at most two sources among inputs, earlier gates, and constants. Proof: induction on prefix length; the filtering step retains precisely those descriptions that also agree at the next position. This is an explicit exponential-in-s procedure, not a polynomial-in-s bound.

label: S0011
statement:
statement: Finite-list range avoidance lemma. Let N,K be integers with 0 <= K < 2^N, and let L be an explicitly enumerable list of K (not necessarily distinct) strings in {0,1}^N. There is a deterministic algorithm that outputs y in {0,1}^N absent from L using O(NK) inspections of list bits, plus the cost of enumerating L, and O(N) working bits beyond the list enumerator. At each position extend the current prefix by the bit whose resulting prefix occurs in at most half as many list entries as the current prefix. After i positions at most K/2^i list entries match; after N positions this is <1, hence zero.
evidence: Proof: Initially all K list entries match the empty prefix. Given a prefix matched by q entries, the counts matching its 0- and 1-extensions sum to q, so one extension has count at most q/2. Induction gives at most K/2^i matches after i choices. At i=N the count is at most K/2^N<1 and is an integer, hence 0. To implement, scan the explicit list for each step and count the two next-bit values among entries matching the current prefix; this uses O(NK) bit inspections and stores the prefix and counters in O(N) bits. Duplicate list entries do not affect the argument. For circuit truth tables this only yields the corresponding cost after enumerating the circuit descriptions; it does not establish polynomial time at the CJSW threshold, so G0001 remains open.

statement: statement: Restricted uniform range-refuter theorem. Fix a constant c>0. For each n>=2 let N=2^n and s<=c n/log_2(n+2). In the ordered fan-in-two Boolean circuit model over AND, OR, NOT, with n named inputs, constants 0 and 1, at most s gates, and any available wire as output, a deterministic algorithm outputs an N-bit truth table outside the size-s circuit image in time polynomial in N. Proof: put W=n+s+2. For each k<=s, there are at most (3W^2)^k gate lists and at most W output choices, so the number K of descriptions is at most W sum_{k=0}^s(3W^2)^k <= (s+1)W(3W^2)^s. Since s=O(n/log n) and log W=O(log n), log_2 K=O(log n)+O(s log n)=O(n), hence K<=N^C for a constant C depending on c. Enumerate all descriptions, including duplicates in their truth tables. The explicit-list prefix-halving construction produces a table absent from this list using N scans and O(NK) list-bit inspections. Each table can be generated by evaluating its circuit on all N inputs in O(N(s+1)) Boolean-gate operations. Thus total time is O(N^2 K(s+1)) plus polynomial description-enumeration overhead, which is polynomial in N. The output is outside the circuit image because the prefix procedure leaves zero list entries matching it. This theorem only covers s=O(n/log n); it does not establish a refuter for every superpolylogarithmic-in-N size threshold required by the CJSW route.

statement: PROCEDURE R2 (deterministic restriction by conditional expectations; repair of the refuted every-z form). Setting as in S0006: w_ji in {-1,+1}, |A|=k, f=n-k>=1, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Since the non-constancy of gate j on {0,1}^A depends only on the offset S_j(z) (A-weights and t_j are fixed), N(A,z) = #{j : S_j(z) in W_j}, where W_j is a set of at most k integers (S0006 step 1). Let F_r(p) = sum_j P[S_j in W_j | first r bits of z equal p], for a prefix p of length r. Then (i) F_r(p) = (F_{r+1}(p0)+F_{r+1}(p1))/2; (ii) each F_r(p) is an exact finite sum: given p, S_j = a_j(p) + (signed Bin(f-r,1/2)), so P[S_j in W_j | p] = sum over s in W_j of the binomial pmf at the shifted index. Algorithm: start with the empty prefix; at each of the f steps append the bit b minimising F_{r+1}(pb). By (i), F is non-increasing along the path, so the output z* satisfies N(A,z*) = F_f(z*) <= F_0 = sum_j P[S_j in W_j] <= m k / sqrt(f) (S0006). Running time: f steps, each O(m k f) exact arithmetic (rational with denominator 2^f, or exact integers), so poly(n, m). Scope: +-1 weights; the output is ONE restriction z*, not a CAPP algorithm.

statement: PROCEDURE (CLAIMED, not reviewed). Algorithm: keep a table indexed by S = (S_1..S_k), S_c = sum over processed variables q of w_{c,q} x_q. Start with {(0,..,0): 1}. For variable i = 1..n and each b in {0,1}, add w_{c,i} b to every coordinate S_c and accumulate counts. Output the sum of table counts over final S with sum_j v_j [S_{c(j)} >= t_j] >= T. Correctness: [w_c . x >= t] = [S_c(x) >= t], so F(x) = G(S(x)) for a fixed function G. By induction, after i variables the table maps each S to the number of length-i prefixes with partial sums S. Summing over final S gives sum_x [G(S(x)) >= T] = #F. Bound: after i steps each S_c lies in [-Wi, Wi], so the table has at most (2Wi+1)^k entries and the total time is O(n (2Wn+1)^k (k+m)) arithmetic operations. Scope of consequence: for k <= eps n / log2(2Wn+1), the time is 2^{eps n} poly(n, m, W), so #SAT of THR o THR with at most k distinct bottom weight vectors is computed in 2^{eps n} poly time. No claim for k = m (all bottom weight vectors distinct).

statement: PROOF. Every gate is either supported in V2 (all gates with |supp| >= 2, and unary gates on V2) or a unary gate on a variable of V1; no unary gate sits on V0. A unary gate on i equals b0 + (b1 - b0) x_i with b1 - b0 in {-1,0,1}, so the top sum equals S(y) + c + sum_i a_i z_i, where y is the V2 part and z the V1 part of x. statement: statement: Let S_1,...,S_m be pairwise disjoint supports, k_j=|S_j|, and let gate j be an integer threshold predicate on S_j with integer top weight v_j. Given T, the satisfying-assignment count can be computed in O(sum_j k_j 2^{k_j} + m(V+1)) arithmetic operations, where V=sum_j |v_j|, and O(V+1) coefficient storage, after processing the factors in the signed-weight generating-function identity. statement: For every n>=1 and integer s>=0, in the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model over {AND,OR,NOT} with n named inputs and one output, there is a uniform deterministic procedure that outputs a truth table outside the size-s circuit image, using at most 2^{2^n} * 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))} * 2^n time and 2^{2^n} bits of working storage, provided the circuit image is proper. Proof: Enumerate every n-bit truth table in lexicographic order as a candidate. For each candidate, enumerate all circuit descriptions with at most s gates, evaluate each on all 2^n inputs, and compare its output table with the candidate. Output the first candidate unmatched by every enumerated circuit. Evaluating one circuit takes O((s+1)2^n) operations. The candidate loop has 2^{2^n} iterations. Every size-s circuit is enumerated, and properness guarantees an unmatched candidate. structure.lemma: Bounded-form DP. Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates, each bottom gate j computing [w_j.x >= t_j] with integer weights |w_j,i| <= B, and suppose the bottom linear forms take at most r distinct values w^(1),...,w^(r) (as vectors). Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(n * m * (2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations. Proof: process variables x_1..x_n in order; after prefix i the state is the vector s(i) in [-Bi,Bi]^r of partial sums w^(k)_{[1..i]}.x_{[1..i]}. The contribution of the remaining variables to each form depends only on s(i) and the suffix, so the number of partial assignments with a given state can be accumulated in a map state -> count with at most (2Bi+1)^r <= (2Bn+1)^r entries; each entry has 2 successors. At the end each bottom gate j is [s^(k(j)) >= t_j] for its form index k(j), so the top gate value is a function of the final state, evaluated in O(m) per entry. Total O(n (2Bn+1)^r) map operations plus O(m (2Bn+1)^r) top-gate evaluations, i.e. O(n m (2Bn+1)^r). Consequence: for B constant and r <= delta' n / log2(2Bn+1) with delta' < 1, the running time is 2^{(1-delta)n} poly(n) for some delta > 0. Scope: stated subclass (few distinct bottom forms). It does NOT cover generic THR o THR, where r = m = n^1.5 (lab: distinct bottom forms at r = m; bottom-pattern ratio to 2^n stays 0.88-0.97 at n=10-14, cm-4742a666e39f408c and cm-bc1e1e36b02c443f). Open: G0001 (generic instances), and whether a reduction shrinks the number of distinct forms.

(A x) for j in N, and W_X x = E x, so f(x) = [sum_{j in N} v_j [C_j.(Ax) >= t_j] + sum_q v_{X,q} [(Ex)_q >= t_{X,q}] >= T] is a function of s(x) alone. Let c(y,z) = #{x in {0,1}^n : s(x) = (y,z)}. statement: PROCEDURE (affine enumeration for positive 1-in-3 SAT). Let S be a positive 1-in-3 clause set on variables 1..n with incidence matrix A in {0,1}^{m x n}, and V = {x in F_3^n : Ax = 1 mod 3}. (i) S is satisfiable iff V contains a point of {0,1}^n. Proof: (=>) a 1-in-3 solution has every clause sum exactly 1, so Ax = 1 mod 3. (<=) for a 0/1 vector each clause sum lies in {0,1,2,3}, and the only element congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1, so every clause sum equals 1. (ii) Gaussian elimination over F_3 on [A|1] either reports V empty or gives V = x0 + ker A with k = n - rank_3(A); enumerating the 3^k points and testing 0/1 membership decides S in time O(mn^2 + 3^k mn). statement: Lemma (constructive halving for finite image prefixes). Let D be a finite set of descriptions, |D|<=2^m, each specifying a Boolean string in a fixed coordinate order. There is a deterministic sequential procedure that outputs a length-(m+1) string outside the set of length-(m+1) prefixes specified by D. Proof: maintain the descriptions agreeing with the prefix so far. At coordinate i, partition the live set by output bit 0 or 1, choose a bit whose part has smaller cardinality (tie-break 0), and retain only that part. Each step halves the live set, so after m+1 steps its size is at most 2^m/2^(m+1)<1. The output prefix is therefore specified by no description. If each description is an s-gate circuit encoding and its i-th output can be evaluated in poly(s) time, scanning all descriptions at each step gives O(2^m poly(s)) time per update and O(2^m) bits of storage. This constructs an avoidance witness but does not give a polynomial update bound or a reduction from bounded one-pass Search-MCSP.

statement: Lemma (preprocessed trie range avoidance). Let D be a finite multiset of Boolean strings of common length N, with |D|<=2^m. Given the complete binary prefix trie of D annotated at each node by the number of D-strings extending its prefix, one can deterministically output a length-(m+1) prefix not extended by any member of D using O(m) node inspections and O(m) working bits. Proof: start at the root. At each level i<=m+1, if either child has count zero, choose that child and stop; its prefix has no extension in D. Otherwise choose a child with minimum count (ties to 0). If no zero child was encountered, induction gives count at depth i at most |D|/2^i<=2^(m-i). At depth m+1 this is <1, and as an integer the count is zero. Each step inspects at most two child counts and emits one bit, so there are O(m) inspections and O(m) output/work storage. This proves fast construction only after the trie and counts are supplied; forming and storing them is not bounded by the lemma and may cost Theta(|D|N).

statement: Finite-language residual-state lemma and exact recognizer: For any finite L subseteq {0,1}^N with K=|L|, at every cut t, the number of distinct residuals R_t={ {q in {0,1}^{N-t}: pq in L}: p in {0,1}^t } is at most 2^K. Moreover L has a deterministic one-pass recognizer whose state is a K-bit indicator of which words of L agree with the prefix read so far; each update uses at most K fan-in-two AND gates plus one shared input complement, and the final state accepts iff any indicator remains set.
proof: Write L={w_1,...,w_K}. For each length-t prefix p define I_p={i: w_i begins with p}. Its residual L_p is exactly the set of suffixes after position t of w_i for i in I_p. Thus L_p is determined by I_p subseteq [K], so there are at most 2^K residuals. For recognition, initialize K indicators to 1. At position j on input bit b, replace indicator i by indicator_i AND [w_i[j]=b]. By induction, after j positions indicator i is 1 exactly when w_i agrees with the input prefix. At j=N some indicator remains 1 exactly for inputs in L. Store a fixed witness label with each w_i and output one associated label if accepted, otherwise none. Each update uses one conjunction per indicator; comparisons to fixed bits use b or its shared complement. This proves the finite-language lemma and procedure only; it gives no useful lower bound for Search-MCSP when K is large.
